name: Employer-Sponsored Work Permit

requirements.blocker_text: Under the General Law of Migration (Ley 370), an employer must first obtain Ministry of Labour approval for the work permit, which requires demonstrating the position cannot be filled by a local candidate (a labor-market test). Bolivian labor law caps foreign staff at 15% of any company's workforce (equivalently, at least 85% Bolivian nationals). The employee separately obtains a Specific Purpose Visa (valid 30 days for entry) at a Bolivian consulate, then registers with DIGEMIG for biometric processing and obtains a Foreigner's Identity Card. The employer must also register the employee with the public health system (Caja Nacional de Salud) and pension system.
requirements.fix_path: Secure a job offer from an employer that has not exceeded its 15% foreign-staff cap, obtain Ministry of Labour approval, then apply for the Specific Purpose Visa and complete DIGEMIG registration on arrival.

sources.title: GoResident -- Ley 370, Ministry of Labour labor-market test, 15% foreign-staff cap, process steps, fees, validity

STATUS: DRAFT -- migracion.gob.bo returned a certificate/hostname-mismatch SSL error on every attempt in this build (a distinct failure mode from the usual robots-block or timeout seen elsewhere in this dataset), so this rests on a tier-3 relocation-services summary. GENUINE FINDING, a real structural feature not seen in most countries built so far in this dataset: a hard, numeric foreign-staff quota (85% Bolivian / 15% foreign) combined with a labor-market test -- a stricter double-gate similar to Kosovo's quota-plus-labor-market-test combination found earlier in this dataset. work_rights set to 'restricted' since the permit is tied to the sponsoring employer and position. dual_citizenship_allowed set to true here per Article 143 of the 2009 Constitution (confirmed via a tier-3 secondary source in this build; the primary constitutional text fetch for this specific article was incomplete, see py_citizenship_naturalisation.json's Bolivia-equivalent file for the full citation discussion).
